excerpt: Turquoise pools, an 18-meter rappel and cash-only entry: what to know before visiting the Minas Viejas Waterfalls in El Naranjo, San Luis Potosí.
contentHtml:
The Minas Viejas Waterfalls (Cascadas de Minas Viejas) are a system of stepped waterfalls in the municipality of El Naranjo, San Luis Potosí, in the Huasteca Potosina region, and they're one of the most complete nature destinations in northeastern Mexico. Every year, thousands of travelers come to Minas Viejas with the same question: is it worth the trip from Ciudad Valles or from Mexico City? The short answer is yes, but the details matter: the entrance isn't clearly signposted, payment is cash only, and rappelling—the star activity—sells out in high season before 11 in the morning.

Here's the experience: the pools, the rappel and what's good to know before you go. Up-to-date admission, hours and directions are on the Minas Viejas Waterfalls page.

This guide answers exactly those questions. You'll find how to get to the Minas Viejas waterfalls from different starting points, updated prices for 2026, which activities are available for your budget and in which months the water flow is at its best.

At www.huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and tour operators in the region. This guide is updated with the real experiences of people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: November 2026. If you'd rather have someone else handle the logistics, take a look at our all-inclusive packages to visit Minas Viejas.

What the Minas Viejas Waterfalls are and why visit El Naranjo, SLP

What makes the Minas Viejas Waterfalls different from other waterfalls?

Minas Viejas isn't a single waterfall: it's a route of about 1.5 km that links several natural turquoise pools at different levels, each with a water temperature of around 22 °C all year round. Unlike waterfalls such as Tamasopo—where the circuit is more linear—here you climb up and down between pools, cross wooden walkways and can choose to swim, simply take in the view or rappel down the main drop of about 18 meters. The surrounding tropical dry forest and the constant sound of water make it a place of dense, authentic nature.

The groups we coordinate in the Huasteca Potosina agree that the main difference is how physically you interact with the water: here you don't just look from viewpoints; you get into the pools, swim between the falls and, if you booked the rappel, lower yourself on a rope straight down the biggest waterfall. Book the Stepped Paradise tour (Minas Viejas and Micos) with a guide included so you don't waste time at the entrance.

El Naranjo, SLP: the base town for the adventure

The municipality of El Naranjo, San Luis Potosí, is the gateway you have to go through to reach Minas Viejas. The town has basic services—a gas station, pharmacies, and Banco Azteca and Bancomer ATMs—that you should use before heading to the waterfalls, since there's no ATM or card payment inside the natural area. The distance from downtown El Naranjo to the waterfalls entrance is about 8 km on a paved road in good condition.

If you're planning to combine destinations, you can also visit the Micos Waterfalls from Ciudad Valles, 20 min from the city. The Stepped Paradise tour visits both in a single day. Pairing the two on the same weekend is one of the most popular routes among travelers passing through Ciudad Valles.

How much does Minas Viejas cost? 2026 prices and activities

A complete breakdown of Minas Viejas prices in 2026

First-time visitors to Minas Viejas tend to underestimate the total cost because the entrance fee looks low. General admission for adults is $100 MXN in 2026, while children ages 2 to 5 and seniors with an INAPAM card (Mexico's senior citizen ID) pay $50 MXN. This fee includes the life jacket—required for swimming in the pools—and access to restrooms. If you add the rappel, the cost goes up to $600 MXN per adult or $400 MXN per child, and parking costs an extra $50 MXN for small cars and $100 MXN for buses. Keep in mind that the whole area is cash only.

For groups who'd rather not handle every detail separately, our Stepped Paradise tour (Paraíso Escalonado) combines Minas Viejas and Micos in one day for $1,600 MXN per person, with transportation from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles, breakfast, admission fees and a certified guide. Check the available options at see available tours in the Huasteca Potosina. The weather can affect whether the rappel is running: after heavy rain, operators suspend the activity for safety without advance notice, which happens often between June and September.

Rappelling at Minas Viejas: what to know before you pay

Rappelling at Minas Viejas is the activity people get most excited about and also the one most often misunderstood. The drop where it's done is about 18 meters high, and you descend down the face of the waterfall with water pouring over you. The on-site operator provides the gear—harness, helmet and rope—and the briefing beforehand takes 10 to 15 minutes. No experience is needed, but you do have to be over 10 years old and weigh less than 120 kg. In high season the available spots sell out before noon, so arriving after 10:00 a.m. in July or August means a real risk of missing out.

If you're looking for other adrenaline experiences in the region, rafting on the Tampaón River is the natural next step for anyone who's already done the rappel and wants to keep up the intensity. You can combine both activities on the same weekend from Ciudad Valles.

Practical tips before visiting the Minas Viejas Waterfalls

Preparing well for Minas Viejas makes the difference between a smooth visit and one full of setbacks. The ground is wet, some stretches have slippery rock, and the sun beats down hard between 11:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. These are the most useful tips, based on the experience of the groups we accompany every season in the Huasteca Potosina:

  • Bring cash only: There's no ATM in the natural area. Withdraw money in El Naranjo before you go. Budget at least $800 MXN per adult if you plan to rappel, grab something to eat and pay for parking.
  • Arrive before 9:00 a.m. in high season: In July and August, the parking lot fills up before 10:00 a.m. Getting there early also guarantees you a rappel spot. Check the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina for the month of your trip.
  • Wear water shoes or sandals with good grip: The rocks inside the pools and on the trails are covered in algae and moss. Beach flip-flops without a back strap are a real hazard. Bring a second pair of dry shoes for the ride back.
  • Biodegradable sunscreen only: Since 2024, access to the pools requires sunscreen free of chemicals that harm the aquatic ecosystem. Staff at the entrance check it. If you bring regular sunscreen, you'll have to rinse off before getting in the water.
  • Work out your total trip budget ahead of time: If you combine Minas Viejas with other destinations on the route, the cost per person can vary quite a bit. The guide on how much the Huasteca Potosina costs in 2026 breaks down every expense by destination so you can plan without surprises.
  • Check your bag before you leave: Swimsuit, microfiber towel, dry bag for your phone, biodegradable sunscreen and drinking water are the things travelers forget most. The packing checklist for the jungle of San Luis Potosí is a handy reference so you don't forget anything.

How do you get to Minas Viejas from Ciudad Valles and other cities?

How to get to the Minas Viejas waterfalls is the most common question among travelers planning the trip for the first time. Its location in El Naranjo, SLP, makes it reachable from several points in the Huasteca Potosina, but the entrance isn't always well signposted and navigation apps often get the last stretch wrong. The groups we take every season recommend saving the GPS coordinates before you leave: 22°35′N, 99°17′W (main entrance to Minas Viejas).

Route from Ciudad Valles to Minas Viejas

From Ciudad Valles, take Highway 70 north and turn off toward El Naranjo on Highway 80. It's about 95 km and 1 hour 45 minutes by car. The route is fully paved and doable in any type of vehicle. When you reach El Naranjo, take the marked turnoff to the waterfalls—about 8 km more—on a local road in good condition. Don't rely only on Google Maps for that last stretch; ask at the town's gas station for exact directions. Check out our Minas Viejas and Micos tour if you'd rather have transportation included from Ciudad Valles.

Transportation options to get to Minas Viejas

There's no direct public transportation from Ciudad Valles to the waterfalls entrance, but Vencedor and Grupo Senda buses cover the Ciudad Valles–El Naranjo route, with frequent departures starting at 6:00 a.m. A ticket costs around $80–$100 MXN per person in 2026. From El Naranjo, you'll need a mototaxi or local taxi to reach the waterfalls, for about $50–$80 MXN per ride. The most comfortable option for families or groups of more than four is still your own car or an organized tour, which includes round-trip transportation from the main towns in the Huasteca Potosina.

Frequently asked questions about Minas Viejas

How much time do you need to visit the Minas Viejas Waterfalls?

A full visit to Minas Viejas, including the walk through all the pools, time to swim and the rappel, takes 3 to 4 hours. If you only walk the pools without rappelling, 2 hours is enough. We recommend arriving at 8:00 a.m. and leaving before 1:00 p.m. to avoid the peak crowds.

How much is admission to Minas Viejas in 2026?

General admission to Minas Viejas is $100 MXN per adult and $50 MXN for children ages 2 to 5 and seniors with an INAPAM card. The rappel costs $600 MXN for adults / $400 MXN for children. Parking costs an extra $50–$100 MXN. The whole area is cash only.

When is the best time to visit Minas Viejas, and when does it have the most water?

The waterfalls have water all year, but the flow peaks between July and October, after the rainy season. If you want fewer crowds and still good water levels, October and November are the ideal months. In the dry season (March–May), the water level drops noticeably, although the site is still worth visiting. Avoid Minas Viejas during Holy Week (Semana Santa) if you can't stand crowds.

Is it safe to bring young children to the Minas Viejas Waterfalls?

Minas Viejas is suitable for families with children over 5 years old who know how to swim. Life jackets are required for everyone in the pools and come with your admission. For children under 5, walking the trail to look at the falls is possible, but getting in the water requires constant supervision. The rappel is available for kids over 10 years old.
